targets.text: culture-nodes officially supports Qwen Code as a fourth actor backend: adapters/qwen ships qwen-bridge, a PRD-13 actor-protocol implementation that drives Qwen Code over ACP (qwen --acp, stdio JSON-RPC), with the container image as the support contract (#113) and the configured repository as the agent's identity (#114), running on spark/thor/orin where qwen 0.22.0 already lives

the exported spec names adapters/qwen as a fourth PRD-13 reference implementation driven over ACP, and its boundaries read back as image-contract (#113) + repo-config (#114); verify by reading docs/specs/qwen-bridge-acp.md after export and diffing its claims against this frame

qwen-bridge is the fourth reference implementation of the PRD 13 actor protocol: a standalone package at adapters/qwen (own pyproject, tests, README, Dockerfile), mirroring the sibling layout field for field; it passes tests/conformance unmodified and emits proposed-only ledger authority (provenance: api/actor-protocol/README.md provider-neutral clause + adapters/{claude-code,colleague,codex} layout)
the adapters/qwen package mirrors the sibling layout module-for-module and the conformance kit runs against it UNMODIFIED; verify by a green tests/conformance run in the qwen adapter's CI job

terminal-event discipline carries over: a qwen process that exits 0 without an explicit ACP terminal session event is incomplete and maps to an execution failure, never ok; only Qwen's own completed-session event (with no failure event before it) counts as a completed turn (provenance: adapters/codex/README.md load-bearing crash case + tests/test_codex_cli.py exit-zero rule)

a qwen process that exits without a terminal session/prompt event is classified incomplete and the run reports execution failure, never ok; verify by a qwen-suite test reproducing the codex-bridge crash case (exit 0, no terminal event) asserting incomplete

no PRD-13 wire-protocol change: the actor contract is provider-neutral and input is opaque JSON; qwen-specific knobs (model, ACP flags, approval policy) ride on input fields the bridge itself defines, exactly as codex rides sandbox/model (provenance: api/actor-protocol/README.md + adapters/codex/README.md invocation-input table)
the PRD-13 wire contract stays untouched: no diff in api/actor-protocol/README.md or tests/conformance from this work; verify by git diff of those paths after implementation

the image IS the support contract (issue #113): qwen-bridge ships a pinned Dockerfile (node + qwen-code install + stdlib-only python bridge), a stated toolchain contract, a CI build, and documented build+run; a qwen backend on a host without the image is unsupported (provenance: issue #113 body via agtag issue fetch, 2026-08-23)

the qwen-bridge image is buildable from a pinned Dockerfile (node + qwen-code versions stated), CI-built, and qwen-bridge refuses to serve invokes when the contract leg is missing; verify by the documented build+boot run and a negative boot test

the repository IS the agent's configuration (issue #114): the image carries no agent identity; at startup the bridge consumes culture.yaml + prompt file + skills from the configured repo, refuses to start with a distinct message when any leg is missing, and reports the loaded config repo + revision on the capability surface in the #96 shape (provenance: issue #114 body via agtag issue fetch, 2026-08-23)

the bridge loads culture.yaml + prompt file + skills from the configured repository at startup, refuses with DISTINCT messages per missing leg, and reports the loaded config repo + revision on the capability surface; verify by three negative tests (one per leg) plus an assertion on the capability document contents

host drift is measured, not assumed: the capability surface reports the bundled node version (measured drift: spark bundles v22.23.2 vs thor v18.19.1 under the SAME qwen 0.22.0), the qwen install layout, and PATH independence (qwen is not on the non-interactive ssh PATH on thor/orin - the image entrypoint must not rely on it) (provenance: ssh probes, 2026-08-23; issue #96 toolchain discipline as cited by #113)

the capability surface reports measured host facts - qwen version, bundled node version, model identity, context budget - not assumed defaults; verify by booting on spark/thor/orin and diffing the capability documents against the 2026-08-23 probes (node v22.23.2 vs v18.19.1; NVFP4-27B vs cortex)

the spec's readers: (1) the engineer implementing adapters/qwen, (2) the operators deploying the qwen-bridge image on the spark/thor/orin fleet, (3) the control plane and the nodes CLI users who will schedule qwen actors and read its preflight capability surface

a fresh implementer can answer who/what/where from the spec alone, without re-deriving the fleet facts; verify by having a new agent session state the audience, the seam, and the three host constraints from docs/specs/qwen-bridge-acp.md only

Qwen Code runs on the fleet as an ad-hoc session surface (spark/thor/orin, qwen 0.22.0 measured 2026-08-23) but is NOT a supported actor backend of culture-nodes: there is no adapters/qwen, no container image, no preflight capability surface - qwen invocations have no PRD-13 lifecycle (no callbacks, no idempotent replay, no cancellation, no ledger authority) and the support question 'do we officially support this agent' has no answer for qwen

the absence of today is real, not imagined: no adapters/qwen directory, no qwen image target, no qwen capability surface in the control plane; verify by ls adapters, the image-build matrix, and the preflight actor list before implementation

adapters/qwen ships qwen-bridge - a fourth PRD-13 reference implementation that passes tests/conformance unmodified, speaks the ACP client seam (initialize / session/new / session/prompt / session/cancel over stdio, classified by the terminal session/prompt response, not by exit code), boots from a pinned Dockerfile carrying node + qwen-code (#113 image contract) with the configured repository as its identity (#114), and advertises a preflight capability surface reporting measured host facts (qwen version, bundled node version, model identity, context budget)
every after_state leg is checkable as a command: conformance run, image boot + capability fetch, one synthetic invoke; verify by running those three commands after implementation

every other schedulable backend (claude-code, colleague, codex) already has a containerized, contract-gated bridge, while qwen is the surface this repo's own session work runs on today - and the fleet is heterogeneous (measured: bundled node v22.23.2 vs v18.19.1 under the same qwen 0.22.0; models NVFP4-27B vs cortex) - so without the bridge + image + capability surface, qwen work stays unsupported, host-drift-prone, and invisible to the preflight gate

the heterogeneity driving this work is measured, not asserted: the 2026-08-23 fleet probes (node version drift, model identity split, PATH absence) are reproducible on demand; verify by re-running the three ssh probes

the conformance kit passes against qwen-bridge with 0 failures; the pinned image boots and serves a preflight capability document on all 3/3 fleet hosts; a synthetic PRD-13 invoke returns a terminal-event-classified result; and 0 crashes are classified ok - the codex-bridge crash case (exit 0, no terminal event) is reproduced as a passing test in the qwen suite
each success-signal token maps to a runnable check with a stated threshold (0 failures, 3/3 hosts, 0 crashes-as-ok); verify by the commands named in the spec producing those exact numbers

classifier grounded on MEASURED terminal shapes (challenge probe2, 2026-08-23): stopReason end_turn -> ok (a tool-level failure still ends end_turn with error null - the tool failure rides in the transcript, not the run status, as measured); stopReason cancelled -> the 13 cancellation outcome; a JSON-RPC error on the session/prompt response -> error; no terminal response (process death/timeout) -> incomplete, never ok (provenance: /tmp/acp-probe2 measurements - failing cat ended end_turn; cancelled list turn ended stopReason cancelled error null)

the measured shapes are replayable: a failing-tool turn ends end_turn with error null and a cancelled turn ends stopReason cancelled - verified by the qwen suite test that synthesizes both terminal responses and asserts ok and the 13 cancellation outcome respectively, and by re-running the probe2 script while the evidence exists on spark

the ACP session mode is qwen's approval-policy surface: measured modes are plan (analyze only, no files/commands), default (approval-gated), auto-edit, auto (classifier-approved) with currentModeId defaulting to auto in a scratch session; the bridge maps input.sandbox + the preflight gate onto mode selection, fails closed (never a silently-wider mode), and reports the effective mode on the capability surface - this is the concrete candidate mapping for parked v3 (provenance: challenge probe2 session/new responses, 2026-08-23)

the mode mapping is verified per mode before the bridge relies on it: a plan-mode session refuses a shell command (measured refusal, not a silent no-op) and the capability surface reports the effective mode - until then the bridge sets the mode from the input/preflight policy and never falls back to the measured default auto

the bridge validates the initialize handshake before serving: the negotiated protocolVersion must be supported (measured: 1), agentInfo.version is recorded (measured: qwen-code 0.22.0), and a disagreement fails closed with a distinct message - because qwen 0.22.0 still advertises --acp alongside --experimental-acp, ACP is treated as an experimental seam: the image pins the qwen version and the conformance suite pins the handshake shape (provenance: challenge probe2 initialize response + qwen --help flag pair, 2026-08-23)

an unsupported handshake is refused: verified by a unit test feeding the measured initialize response with protocolVersion 2 (or agentInfo.version mismatch) and asserting the distinct refusal message before any session is served

qwen's model credentials and endpoint configuration are host-supplied (measured authMethods include an OPENAI_API_KEY env path; this fleet uses per-host settings.json endpoints) and are NEVER baked into the image or the configured repository; the capability surface reports the config source and model identity without reporting values (provenance: challenge probe2 initialize authMethods + the measured per-host model.name split, 2026-08-23)

no credentials in the image or the config repo: verified by grepping the built image filesystem for key material and asserting the capability document names the config source (env or settings path) without its values

the 13 result payload carries a DOWNSAMPLED transcript - final assistant text, tool_call summaries with measured statuses (pending/in_progress/failed), usage_update totals - not the raw session/update firehose (measured ~72 notifications for one simple turn, dominated by thought chunks); the full stream is retained in the bridge's local transcript file for debugging (provenance: challenge probes 1+2 stream counts, 2026-08-23)

the result payload stays small: verified by asserting the payload for a turn measured at ~72 session/update notifications is <= 64 KB, against the bridge's local transcript file which retains the full stream

tasks.summary: Port the 19-module shared core into the adapters/qwen package
acceptance_criteria: the package imports cleanly and the ported core test suite runs green (0 failures) under uv run --project adapters/qwen pytest -q

preflight.py is byte-identical to the codex sibling's (a committed diff test asserts it; if tests/lint/preflightsurface_test.go enumerates bridges explicitly, the list gains qwen and the Go lint passes with all four surfaces equal)
the c12 absence check is recorded: ls adapters shows no qwen entry and .github/workflows contains no adapter-qwen.yml before t6 (the thor actor-list leg is dispositioned to t8 per c22)
tasks.instruction: Copy the module set from adapters/codex/src/codex_bridge (the 19-module core) into adapters/qwen/src/qwen_bridge, renaming the package only; do NOT copy codex_cli.py (t2 writes qwen_cli.py in its place). Port the codex core tests, re-aimed at the qwen package. The design source of truth is docs/specs/2026-08-23-qwen-bridge-acp.md (c2/c12/h9).

tasks.summary: Build qwen_cli.py: the ACP client seam and the terminal-event classifier
acceptance_criteria: the classifier maps the measured terminal shapes with one passing test each: stopReason end_turn -> ok (including the tool-failure fixture where a failed cat still ends end_turn with error null), stopReason cancelled -> the 13 cancellation outcome, a JSON-RPC error on the session/prompt response -> error, no terminal response (fake agent dies) -> incomplete
exit-0-without-terminal-event is asserted incomplete, never ok - the crash-case test mirrors codex's test_codex_cli.py rule

the handshake gate refuses an unsupported protocolVersion or an agentInfo.version mismatch with a distinct message before serving (unit test feeds the measured initialize response with protocolVersion 2)
the result payload for the 72-notification turn fixture is <= 64 KB while the full session/update stream is retained in the bridge's local transcript file

the session mode is set from the input/preflight policy at session creation and never falls back to the measured default auto; the effective mode is exposed to the capability surface; the h14 named probe (kill process, session/load the recorded sessionId) is a committed script whose result is recorded, and continuation_ref is NOT implemented in the first cut
unknown ext methods (the craft/drainMidTurnQueue fixture, id 0) are answered leniently and the turn completes
tasks.instruction: Build test-first against a fake ACP agent: a stdio JSON-RPC script under tests/fixtures/acp/ that replays the MEASURED shapes from the 2026-08-23 probes (scripts /tmp/acp-probe/probe.py and /tmp/acp-probe2/probe2.py on spark - re-run them if absent and regenerate the fixtures). The measured facts: initialize returns protocolVersion 1 + agentInfo qwen-code 0.22.0 + authMethods + agentCapabilities{loadSession:true}; session/new returns sessionId + modes{plan,default,auto-edit,auto}; failed tool calls end end_turn; cancel is a notification answered by stopReason cancelled; the terminal response carries _meta.qwen.branchPoint. The spec's c16/c19/c21 are the classifier contract; the v1 frame decision is the client-obligation contract (no fs/terminal handlers in the first cut). h14 (the resume probe) is a claim-side verification, not a plan target - the committed probe script satisfies it without covering a target.

tasks.summary: qwen capabilities + deployment: the measured host-facts surface
acceptance_criteria: the capability document reports qwen version, bundled node version, model identity, config source (env or settings path, WITHOUT values), and the effective session mode - parsed from the measured initialize response plus qwen --version and node --version fixtures, 0 failures
the context budget is reported only from a measured source; where qwen 0.22.0 does not expose it, the field is null - asserted on the orin/cortex fixture
the deployment leg refuses to serve invokes when a contract leg is missing: the negative boot test boots the bridge without the qwen binary and asserts the distinct message (h5)
tasks.instruction: Parse, never hard-code: the 2026-08-23 probe values (node v22.23.2 vs v18.19.1, unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 vs cortex) are DIFF fixtures for the capability document, not constants in the code. The host-local model fact (c8, a confirmed assumption) is what this surface reports; c20: the measured authMethods (OPENAI_API_KEY env path) + per-host settings.json endpoints are the config source the surface names without leaking. Spec c10/c20 are the contract.

tasks.summary: config.py: the #114 configured-repo load, fail-closed per leg
acceptance_criteria: the bridge loads the culture.yaml + AGENTS.md + .qwen/skills triple from the configured repository at startup, and three negative tests (one per missing leg) assert three DISTINCT refusal messages with no invoke served
the capability document carries the loaded config repo + revision (the clone HEAD), asserted against a fixture clone at a known revision
tasks.instruction: The qwen prompt-file leg is AGENTS.md (the measured qwen context file on this repo). Per issue #114 (spec c7): the image carries no identity; the repo is the config; missing legs refuse with distinct messages (fail closed). The .qwen/skills surface vendored 2026-08-23 (9 lineage-marked skills) is the skills leg this repo would load.

tasks.summary: Bridge entrypoint + 13 integration: invoke/cancel/replay against the fake ACP agent
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/invocations against the fake ACP agent returns 200 with the classified ok result for a completed turn, and a cancelled invoke returns the 13 cancellation outcome - integration tests, 0 failures
an idempotent replay of a finished invoke returns the same result without re-executing the model turn (the fake agent asserts exactly one session/prompt call for the replayed invocation id)

the 202 async path emits the callback sequence (stable invocation id, increasing sequence) against the fake agent, and the every-after_state-leg check runs as commands: conformance-style invoke, boot + capability fetch, synthetic invoke
tasks.instruction: Wire the ported core (dialin/async_runner/callbacks/idempotency/scope_guard/session_registry - already in the package from t1) to qwen_cli (t2) behind the config (t4) and capabilities (t3). Boot the server on a localhost port in tests; the 13 shapes are api/actor-protocol/README.md - do NOT extend them (c5). The entrypoint is src/qwen_bridge/__main__.py so t1's pyproject stays untouched by this task.

tasks.summary: Dockerfile + CI workflow + conformance kit script (the #113 image contract)
acceptance_criteria: the image builds on aarch64 (the measured uniform fleet architecture) and contains node + pinned qwen 0.22.0 + the stdlib-only python bridge; a grep of the built image filesystem finds zero credential material

run_conformance_kit.sh passes against the built image with the kit UNMODIFIED (0 failures), and the workflow mirrors adapter-codex.yml (test + lint + conformance jobs, fake-driven so no real qwen in CI)

the diff check passes: nothing lands outside adapters/qwen, .github/workflows/adapter-qwen.yml, and the docs this task names - api/actor-protocol/ and tests/conformance are byte-identical (git diff assertion in the workflow, enforcing the c9 non-goal)

Copy scripts/run_conformance_kit.sh from a sibling UNMODIFIED. The success-signal commands (c15/h12) are named in the workflow job names so the 0-failures / 3-of-3-hosts tokens map to checks.

risks.text: resume/continuation_ref is OUT of the first cut (frame park v2): the session/load cross-process measurement (h14's named probe) has not been run - any dispatch needing resume stays on the codex/claude-code bridges until it is, and the t2 committed probe script is the named verification

the model/API JSON-RPC error shape is SYNTHESIZED in the t2 suite, not measured live (frame park v4): the only measured failure was a tool failure ending end_turn - the first live occurrence must be captured and diffed against the synthesized fixture before the error leg is trusted

craft/drainMidTurnQueue semantics are unmeasured (frame park v5): the lenient empty-answer is the first-cut behavior (measured to let turns complete) - do not rely on mid-turn queueing until the real handler contract is validated

the mode mapping (c18) is a candidate from the measured session/new modes: h15's per-mode live verification (plan-mode refusing a shell command, etc.) has not been run - the bridge must never fall back to the measured default auto, and the t2 selection logic is tested until h15 passes live
h9's thor control-plane actor-list leg is unmeasured (it lives off-checkout on thor): continuation issue (b) from t8 must run it before the qwen image is declared supported on the fleet
